title: Does it feel easier sharing games?
author: swirllyman
selftext:
I don't mean the actual process of sharing. That has gotten 100x easier without a doubt. I personally just upload to gh-page linked to the project repo (recently setup actions so I can get notifs anytime the new build is finished / ready).
 
What I actually mean is the personal feeling towards sharing your work.. your art.. your creations. Sharing your work is always a vulnerable thing to do, especially with games. Doing AI game dev though, that emotional attachment part just doesn't really exist for me.

I think there is some psychology to be observed here about how making games with AI is results in less emotional attachment towards your work. Maybe because it feels less like your own creation and more like some one else's (shifting blame if it sucks). Maybe it's because you spend significantly less time looking at assets (no longer spending 10.hours staring at that same 2d sprite). Maybe just overall less connection to something that only took you 2-3 hours instead of 2-3 weeks.

Maybe a combo of all 3? 
Idk. I'd be interested in others thoughts on this. When sharing a game made with AI do you feel less emotionally attached to it?

FWIW I also posted a similar post to this in r/indiedev and it's currently getting ROASTED. No surprise there though.

comments.author: E_den
comments.body:
Your other post (not exactly "similar") is absolutely not getting ROASTED on r/IndieDev

Your post makes sense, there's a very high chance AI isn't getting further than a prototype level of quality so it's hard to be attached to a prototype you spent little time on I guess ?

comments.author: MysteriousPepper8908
comments.body: I find it great for working with a team to prototype and come up with concepts. It can be very discouraging to spend a ton of time on an idea and then it's not what the team is into but with AI, I can rapidly prototype until we're kind of on the same page before refining. It's a mixed bag sharing stuff with people that have no investment as they're only going to have so much patience for it so you only tend to share once it gets to a certain point and then you're invested in how it's perceived.
